justification: Core type removed: the nested record moves out of Core to the SPI as eu.exeris.kernel.spi.http.StreamMatch (preview), the carrier StreamRouteResolver returns, so that a driver consuming the resolver and an application or generated handler implementing it name only SPI types (ADR-043 Amendment A1). Code compiled against 0.11 that names HttpRouter.StreamMatch is recompiled against 0.12; the release notes carry the upgrade step. The SPI side of the move is additive, and the SPI compatibility gate diffs exeris-kernel-spi only and does not read this entry.

Core method: it keeps its name and parameters and now returns eu.exeris.kernel.spi.http.StreamMatch, as HttpRouter's implementation of the SPI interface eu.exeris.kernel.spi.http.StreamRouteResolver (ADR-043 Amendment A1). The changed return type changes the method descriptor, so a caller compiled against 0.11 is recompiled against 0.12; the release notes carry the upgrade step. The SPI compatibility gate diffs exeris-kernel-spi only and does not read this entry.

Core method: the descriptor is unchanged, the failure contract is not. A field section over http.maxHeaderListSize or a literal over http.maxStringLiteralSize is now read to its end, applying every dynamic-table insertion and size update and discarding the fields, and fails with HpackDecodingException of kind SIZE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, where it stopped part-way and left the table short of what the client assumed. Every other decode failure keeps kind MALFORMED. The Community HTTP/2 server maps SIZE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED to a 431 stream response and MALFORMED to GOAWAY(COMPRESSION_ERROR), where both were a 400 on an open connection, and AbstractHttp2HeaderLimitTck no longer accepts 400 for an oversized field section. A caller that decodes through HpackDecoder and treats every HpackDecodingException alike keeps compiling and now sees the table in step with the client; one that must tell a refusal from a corrupt block reads HpackDecodingException#kind(). The release notes carry the behaviour change. The SPI compatibility gate diffs exeris-kernel-spi only and does not read this entry.

TCK contract: AbstractCryptoEngineTck gains three cases asserting CryptoProviderConfig#minimumTlsVersion as the handshake floor (a TLS 1.2-only peer refused at the default TLSv1.3, served at TLSv1.2; an unsupported value fails createTlsEngine). They drive a handshake through the new template method bindToSocket, which throws by default, so an existing binding fails them until it implements it or returns false from honoursMinimumTlsVersion() because its provider does not build the TLS context from the configuration. Source-compatible; no SPI class changes.

TCK contract: the three abstract boolean hooks missingDependencyFailsInAllSelector, degradeContinuesOnOptionalFailure and failFastAbortsOnOptionalFailure are replaced by one abstract template method, bootCapturing(List<Subsystem>, boolean, Runnable), which boots the kernel over exactly the subsystems the TCK supplies. The TCK now owns counting probe subsystems and judges the boot by their initialize/start/stop counts and whether kernelMain ran, because a hook that returned a hardcoded true satisfied the previous contract. An existing binding stops compiling until it removes the three overrides and implements bootCapturing, as AbstractSubsystemErrorRoutingTck's bindings do. Source-breaking for bindings; no SPI class changes.

TCK contract: the graph, persistence, HTTP and security provider TCKs (AbstractGraphProviderTck, AbstractPersistenceProviderTck, AbstractHttpProviderTck, AbstractSecurityProviderTck) each gain the template method selectAmong(List), which a binding implements by routing the candidates through its kernel's provider selection. highestPriorityWins stages a rival one priority step above and one below the provider under test, in both discovery orders, and requires that selection to return the highest by identity. selectAmong throws by default, so an existing binding fails highestPriorityWins until it implements it. Source-compatible; no SPI class changes.

Behaviour: the bus an engine returns stamps each publication with the isolation ordinal of the bound KernelProviders.STORAGE_CONTEXT (ADR-101 Ruling 1). A publish under a bound isolation key that is not registered in EventEngine#isolationRegistry() is now refused with EX-EVENT-6009 "unregistered-isolation-key", and a descriptor carrying a non-zero ordinal other than the bound one with "isolation-mismatch"; before 0.13 both were published unscoped. The security interceptor binds a tenant context on every authenticated request, so an application registers every tenant key before publishing under it (MIGRATION.md). No signature changes: EventDescriptor keeps its seven-argument constructor and of(...), and the new members are additive on the preview spi.events package.

TCK contract: the IsolationScoping cases require a binding's engine to return an IsolationKeyRegistry from EventEngine#isolationRegistry() and its bus to implement EventBus#subscribeScoped; both SPI defaults refuse, so a binding that has adopted neither fails those cases until it implements them. Source-compatible; the SPI additions are default methods and an eighth EventDescriptor component behind a retained seven-argument constructor.

Behaviour on the Kafka binding (ADR-101 Ruling 2): a record the Kafka client rejects through the send callback before send returns (an ApiException such as a record too large, or the metadata timeout after max.block.ms) was lost before 0.13: publish returned normally and nothing recorded it. It is now refused with EX-EVENT-6009, as a thrown send already was, and is not counted as published. A send that fails after publish has returned is recorded, never thrown: a KafkaPublishFailedEvent with publishMode "publishAsync" and EventEngineStats#publishFailedTotal. No signature changes: EventEngineStats keeps its seven-argument constructor, which reports 0 for the new component, on the preview spi.events package.

Behaviour: Subsystem#initialize() is bounded by an initialization deadline of 300 s by default (ADR-007 amendment 2026-10-20). A subsystem whose initialize() is still running at the deadline is interrupted, and boot fails with EX-BOOT-0003 (SubsystemInitDeadlineException, rawArgs [subsystemName, deadlineMs]); under DEGRADE an optional subsystem is dropped with its dependents. Before 0.13 such a boot waited indefinitely. KernelBootstrap.Builder#initializeDeadline(Duration) changes the deadline, and Duration.ZERO restores the unbounded wait. The new SPI exception is additive; this Core entry is a record for the release notes, not read by the SPI compatibility gate.

TCK contract: seeds a connected pair through a session and measures findShortestPath(GraphEdgeDescriptor, UUID, UUID); a binding needs a live backend; bootstrapSubsystem throws IllegalStateException unless the engine persists the seeded edges and the three-argument search finds the 2-hop path; source-compatible.

Behaviour on the Community SQL/PGQ binding: connected edges in registered tables are removed; the SPI sentence was already "and all connected edges"; a registered edge table that names the label but whose table name is not a valid SQL identifier makes the call throw GraphQueryException before any statement runs, and one that does not exist in the current scope fails the statement with the persistence engine's translated error; nothing is deleted in either case; no signature change.

Behaviour: boot() registers a JVM shutdown hook that runs KernelBootstrap.shutdown() unless registerShutdownHook(false) is set (ADR-007 section 5); before 0.13 a SIGTERM exited without stopping the subsystems. An embedding host that stops the kernel from its own lifecycle disables the hook in the release that adopts 0.13, or one SIGTERM starts two stop sequences. Subsystem#stop() may now run on a thread that carries none of the kernel's ScopedValue bindings, so a stop() that reads KernelProviders fails there. A second concurrent boot() on one KernelBootstrap instance throws IllegalStateException. No SPI signature changes; this Core entry is a record for the release notes, not read by the SPI compatibility gate.

Behaviour: refuses unconditionally with GraphQueryException (EX-GRPH-5002, queryType SHORTEST_PATH) for distinct and equal ids; deprecated for removal before the graph SPI is promoted; now a default method on the preview SPI interface.
Contract widening: default implementation removed and method made abstract on the preview SPI interface; an out-of-tree implementer must implement this overload directly.

Contract widening: new abstract method on the preview SPI interface for multi-hop path traversal; runs an ordered GraphPathSpec as one request, honours direction, and returns the terminal frontier with walk semantics.
Contract widening: new abstract method on the preview SPI interface streaming the terminal frontier as UTF-8 JSON in a caller-owned LoanedBuffer.
Contract widening: new abstract method on the preview SPI interface generating dialect-specific query text for ordered hops.
Behaviour: direction and bidirectional are honoured on both backends; a descriptor with INCOMING, BOTH, or bidirectional returns reached nodes according to that orientation.
Behaviour: direction and bidirectional are honoured on both backends; equivalent to streamPathJson over a single hop of the traversal's edge.
TCK contract: refusal cases replace the not-found case; the same-node case uses the three-argument overload. The SPI compatibility gate diffs exeris-kernel-spi only and does not read this entry.
TCK contract: new buildPathQuery group exercising multi-hop query generation. The SPI compatibility gate diffs exeris-kernel-spi only and does not read this entry.
